t: AS 10 deals with:
e: AS 10 is Property, Plant and Equipment; AS 7 construction contracts, AS 16 borrowing costs, AS 13 investments.

t: Provision for gratuity and leave encashment of employees is governed by:
e: AS 15 deals with employee benefits including gratuity, pension and leave encashment.

t: Recognition of Deferred Tax Assets and Deferred Tax Liabilities is governed by:
e: AS 22 Taxes on Income deals with deferred tax assets and liabilities.

t: AS 28 deals with:
e: AS 28 is Impairment of Assets; AS 26 is intangibles, AS 27 joint ventures and AS 29 provisions.

t: Keeping the personal transactions of the owners separate from those of the business follows the:
e: The economic entity principle treats the business as separate from its owners.

t: The assumption that the enterprise will continue operating in the foreseeable future is the:
e: The going concern principle assumes continuity of the business, which justifies carrying assets at cost.

t: Total assets of a company are ₹4,200 crore and capital is ₹1,100 crore. Liabilities are:
e: Liabilities = Assets − Capital = 4,200 − 1,100 = ₹3,100 crore.

t: Maintenance of books of account by a company is governed by which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 128 requires books of account to be kept by the company.

t: An officer wants to verify the statutory basis for constituting an Audit Committee. He should refer to:
e: Section 177 deals with the Audit Committee.

t: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is governed by which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with CSR; 138 is internal audit, 149 Board of Directors and 177 Audit Committee.

t: ROC stands for:
e: ROC is the Registrar of Companies under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

t: WACC stands for:
e: WACC is the Weighted Average Cost of Capital.

t: A cheque deposited by the firm is dishonoured by the drawee bank. The effect is:
o: No difference arises between the two books
Pass book balance increases relative to the cash book
Pass book balance decreases relative to the cash book
e: Dishonoured cheques are among the items that decrease the pass book balance or increase the cash book balance.

t: Cash book balance ₹2,00,000. Cheques issued not presented ₹50,000; dividend collected by bank not recorded ₹10,000; cheque deposited dishonoured not recorded ₹25,000; bank charges ₹1,000. Pass book balance is:
From 2018, Ind AS became applicable to non-listed companies having net worth of:
e: Non-listed companies with net worth of ₹500 crore or more were brought under Ind AS.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: The rate of GST applicable on general insurance premium such as motor and fire policies is:
e: General insurance services attract GST at 18%; the GST element is excluded from gross direct premium.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: Under Ind AS 117, the Contractual Service Margin (CSM) represents:
o: The unearned profit on a group of insurance contracts recognised over the coverage period
The reinsurance recoverable on outstanding claims
e: CSM is the unearned profit in a group of contracts that is released to profit as services are provided.

t: Investment functions of insurers are set out in which schedule of the IRDAI AFI Regulations, 2024?
e: Schedule III covers investment functions.

t: Available Solvency Margin is ₹2,700 crore and Required Solvency Margin ₹1,500 crore. The solvency ratio is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Solvency ratio = ASM / RSM = 2,700 / 1,500 = 1.80.

t: Net Premium is also referred to as:
o: Net Written Premium or Net Retained Premium
e: Net premium (GWP less ceded) is the insurer's retention and is also called net written or net retained premium.

t: Premium collected from policyholders ₹3,540 crore including GST of ₹540 crore; reinsurance accepted ₹200 crore; reinsurance ceded ₹800 crore. Net Written Premium is:
Net Written Premium ₹2,400 crore and UPR increased by ₹150 crore during the year. Net Earned Premium is:
e: An increase in UPR reduces earned premium: 2,400 − 150 = ₹2,250 crore.

t: Gross claims paid ₹1,000 crore; opening gross outstanding ₹1,500 crore (including IBNR ₹300 crore); closing gross outstanding ₹1,700 crore (including IBNR ₹350 crore). Gross Incurred Claims are:
e: Outstanding figures already include IBNR: 1,000 + 1,700 − 1,500 = ₹1,200 crore.

t: Gross claims outstanding, for the purpose of computing incurred claims, include:
e: Gross claims outstanding include gross IBNR/IBNER as per the definition of gross incurred claims.

t: Listed equity shares costing ₹120 crore have a fair value of ₹150 crore on the balance sheet date. The ₹30 crore difference is:
o: Credited to the Fair Value Change Account under equity
Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Unrealised gains or losses on actively traded equity are taken to the Fair Value Change Account, not to profit.

t: A claim intimated at a branch on 30 March but not yet entered in the system as on 31 March is covered by:
o: The IBNR reserve, as a claim in transit
e: IBNR includes provision for claims in transit as on the valuation date.

t: Unutilised GST input credit has been outstanding for 150 days. For solvency computation it is:
o: Admissible, as the limit is 365 days
Valued at zero, as the limit is 120 days
Admissible, as the limit is 180 days
e: GST unutilised credit outstanding for more than 120 days is placed at zero value.

t: A balance due from GIC Re has been outstanding for 200 days. For solvency computation the balance is:
o: Valued at zero, as the limit is 90 days
Admissible, as Indian reinsurers' balances are inadmissible only beyond 365 days
Valued at zero, as the limit is 180 days
e: Balances of Indian reinsurers and foreign reinsurers with branches in India are placed at zero only beyond 365 days.

t: The debit balance of the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account is, for solvency purposes:
e: A debit balance of the P&L appropriation account is treated as a zero-value (inadmissible) asset.

t: A Deferred Tax Asset arising on account of accumulated losses is, for solvency computation:
o: Placed at zero value in full
e: DTA arising from accumulated losses is wholly inadmissible; other DTA is 25% admissible.

t: Total DTA ₹60 crore, of which ₹20 crore arises from accumulated losses. The admissible DTA for solvency is:
e: DTA from losses is fully excluded; of the remaining ₹40 crore, 75% is excluded, leaving 25% × 40 = ₹10 crore.

t: Gross Premium ₹2,000 crore with Factor A of 0.85; Net Premium ₹1,600 crore. RSM 1 is:
e: GP × A = 1,700, higher than NP 1,600; RSM 1 = 20% × 1,700 = ₹340 crore.

t: ASM ₹4,500 crore and RSM ₹2,500 crore. The solvency ratio is:
e: Solvency ratio = 4,500 / 2,500 = 1.80.

t: 'Solvency Ratio' is defined as the ratio of:
o: Available Solvency Margin to Required Solvency Margin
e: Solvency ratio = Total ASM / Total RSM.

t: Net written premium of the preceding twelve months: Marine Hull ₹80 crore, Marine Cargo ₹120 crore, Miscellaneous ₹1,000 crore. UPR under the percentage method is:
A branch receives a cheque on 28 March for a policy commencing 5 April. The accountant credits it to premium income of the current year. This is:
o: Correct, as the proposal was accepted
Incorrect; it should be treated as unearned premium reserve
Incorrect; it is premium received in advance and a current liability
Correct, as cash has been received
e: Premium for risks incepting after the accounting period is premium received in advance, shown under current liabilities.

t: Redeemable preference shares held as investments are valued at:
o: Lower of cost or market value
Market value on the balance sheet date
Fair value through the Fair Value Change Account
e: Debt securities including government securities and redeemable preference shares are held to maturity at historical cost.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: Derivative instruments traded in active markets are measured at:
o: Fair value, with unrealised gains/losses taken to the Fair Value Change Account
e: Actively traded equity and derivatives are carried at fair value with changes going to the FVCA under equity.

t: Listed equity costing ₹200 crore has a fair value of ₹170 crore on the balance sheet date. The treatment is:
o: No entry, as the loss is unrealised
₹30 crore debited to the Fair Value Change Account
₹30 crore charged to the Profit and Loss Account
₹30 crore charged to the Revenue Account
e: Unrealised losses on actively traded equity are also taken to the FVCA under equity, not through profit.

t: For all items in the Balance Sheet, Revenue Account and Profit and Loss Account, insurers must show:
o: Budgeted amounts for the next financial year
Corresponding amounts for the immediately preceding financial year
e: The general instructions require comparative figures for the immediately preceding financial year.

t: As per the material, a 'provision' is an amount written off or retained for a known liability or loss whose amount:
o: Cannot be determined with substantial accuracy
Relates to a future contingency only
e: A provision covers a known liability or loss whose amount cannot be determined with substantial accuracy.

t: The Balance Sheet of a general insurer is prepared in:
e: Form B-BS is the balance sheet; the 'B' forms apply to general insurers.

t: Under the Motor segment, separate schedules are prepared for:
o: Motor Own Damage and Motor Third Party
e: Motor is split into sub-segments (a) Motor Own Damage and (b) Motor TP.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

t: Premium received in advance ₹100 crore; unallocated premium ₹50 crore; due to other insurers ₹80 crore; sundry creditors due to policyholders ₹70 crore; outstanding premium ₹120 crore; due from reinsurers ₹90 crore. 'Other liabilities net of other assets' for policyholders' funds is:
e: Other liabilities 300 − other assets 210 = ₹90 crore.

t: Loans and advances granted by an insurer to its employees are:
o: Not admissible for the Available Solvency Margin
e: All such employee loans and advances are inadmissible for ASM.

t: Minimum paid-up equity capital for an insurer carrying on exclusively health insurance business is:
e: Standalone health insurers require ₹100 crore, the same as life and general insurers.

t: Allowable expenses of management computed under the regulations are ₹1,500 crore. The additional allowance for Insurtech and Insurance Awareness expenses is:
e: 5% of the allowable expenses is additionally permitted: 5% × 1,500 = ₹75 crore.

t: URR ₹2,000 crore; reserve for premium deficiency ₹50 crore; reserve for outstanding claims including IBNR/IBNER ₹3,500 crore; net premium ₹3,000 crore. Technical reserves to net premium ratio is:
